correctness.rationale: For n>=1,b>=2, g=gcd(n,b-1), q=(b-1)/g, the digit congruence gives D subset g*N. The residues jn mod (b-1) for j=1..q cover every multiple-of-g residue because gcd(n/g,q)=1. Set T=max_{1<=j<=q} s_b(jn). For any t>=T divisible by g, choose j with s_b(jn)=u congruent t mod (b-1), and apply Clokie et al. Theorem 4 to attain t=u+r(b-1). Carry-free concatenation proves D union {0} additive; scaling gives a numerical semigroup with conductor at most ceil(T/g). Independent finite automaton computed all 1000 admissible targets across 200 (base,modulus) instances.

originality.rationale: The principal infinite tail is a direct corollary of Clokie–Lidbetter–Molina Lovett–Shallit–Witzman Theorem 4 plus the elementary fact that jn covers every gcd-compatible residue modulo b-1. No new nonstandard arithmetic lemma or genuinely narrower unresolved case is required. Concatenation is the standard zero-carry identity, and numerical-semigroup status is the definition once cofinite closure is established. Thus the original claim does not survive the strong prior-implication standard despite absence of identical words in the earlier paper.
residual_risks: This scientific failure is not correctness: the theorem is correct and the finite tests pass. The original packet remains unchanged; no weak disclaimer can make the old originality claim valid.
An explicit named characterization of the full set might be useful pedagogically, but no new exact conductor or substantive independent classification method is established.
